plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: An epiphytic cactus with segmented, flattened stems edged with pointed teeth. It produces vivid tubular flowers at the tips of the stems. It is widely grown as a houseplant in the Northern Hemisphere, where it blooms as nights lengthen.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (November to January)
plants.location: Native to the coastal mountains of southeastern Brazil; cultivated worldwide as a houseplant
plants.funFact: Unlike desert cacti, it grows on trees in humid Brazilian forests. It needs long nights and cool temperatures to set buds, which is why it flowers around Thanksgiving.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large, fast-growing tree with fern-like leaves and dense clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers. In full bloom, the canopy turns purple and carpets the ground with fallen blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa, Australia, Argentina, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacarandas earn it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'. In parts of Australia, the bloom is said to coincide with university exam season.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and delicate, fragrant flowers. It blooms earlier than the common camellia and tolerates more sun, making it a popular hedge and garden plant in warm temperate regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to southern Japan; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Its seeds yield an edible oil used in Japan.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum morifolium
plants.description: A perennial with lobed, aromatic leaves and showy, multi-petaled flower heads in many forms. It is a classic late-autumn bloomer because it flowers in response to shortening days.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (October to December in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to East Asia; cultivated worldwide, especially in China, Japan, and Europe
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums have been cultivated in China for over 2,500 years. Japan's Imperial seal features a stylized chrysanthemum, and the flower is celebrated at an annual festival.
